nodes.label: Domain Model (active discipline)
nodes.rationale: Merely reading CONTEXT.md for vocabulary is not this skill; this is the active discipline of challenging terms and writing the glossary/decisions down the moment they crystallise.

nodes.label: Phase Boundary Decision Tree
nodes.rationale: Five options ordered cheapest/most-precise first (Continue, /clear, /handoff, Subagent, /compact) so the decision is made only at phase boundaries, never mid-phase; compacting mid-phase makes the agent lose the thread.

nodes.label: Primary vs Secondary Source
nodes.rationale: Every move except Continue turns a primary source (the session as it happened) into a lossier secondary source; you only pay that lossiness when staying costs more than it saves.

nodes.label: Fowler Smell Baseline
nodes.rationale: Applies even when the repo documents no standards; the repo's documented standard always overrides the baseline, and each smell is a judgement call, never a hard violation.

nodes.label: PreToolUse Hook
nodes.rationale: Intercepts and blocks dangerous git commands (push, reset --hard, clean -f, branch -D, checkout ./restore .) before Claude executes them.

nodes.label: Dependency Categories
nodes.rationale: Category (in-process, local-substitutable, remote-but-owned, true-external) determines how the deepened module is tested across its seam.

nodes.label: Seam Discipline
nodes.rationale: One adapter means a hypothetical seam; two adapters means a real one, so a port shouldn't be introduced unless at least two adapters are justified.

nodes.label: Replace-Don't-Layer Testing
nodes.rationale: Old unit tests on shallow modules become waste once interface-level tests exist; the interface is the test surface, so tests should survive internal refactors.

nodes.label: Parallel Sub-agent Design Process
nodes.rationale: Spawns 3+ sub-agents each producing a radically different interface, under different constraints (minimize, maximise flexibility, optimise common caller, ports & adapters), because the first idea is unlikely to be the best.

nodes.label: Phase 1: Build Feedback Loop
nodes.rationale: The skill itself: a tight, red-capable, deterministic, fast, agent-runnable pass/fail signal. With it, bisection/hypothesis-testing/instrumentation find the cause; without it, no amount of staring at code helps.

nodes.label: Phase 2: Reproduce + Minimise
nodes.rationale: Shrinking to the smallest scenario that still goes red narrows the hypothesis space and becomes the later regression test.

nodes.label: Phase 3: Hypothesise
nodes.rationale: Generate 3-5 ranked falsifiable hypotheses before testing any, since single-hypothesis generation anchors on the first plausible idea.

nodes.label: Phase 4: Instrument
nodes.rationale: Each probe maps to a specific prediction, changing one variable at a time; tagged debug logs make cleanup a single grep.

nodes.label: Phase 5: Fix + Regression Test
nodes.rationale: Write the regression test before the fix only if a correct seam exists; if no correct seam exists, that absence is itself the finding about the codebase's architecture.

nodes.label: Architecture Decision Record (ADR)
nodes.rationale: Offer only when a decision is hard to reverse, surprising without context, and the result of a real trade-off; value is in recording that and why a decision was made, not filling sections.

nodes.label: CONTEXT.md
nodes.rationale: A tight, opinionated glossary of project-specific terms only; general programming concepts don't belong even if heavily used.
